{"prompt": "My flight got cancelled and I'm stuck at the airport with a connecting flight in 3 hours. What should I do first?", "response": "First, don't wait in the airline's line just yet — call their rebooking phone number or use their app while you're still standing near a gate agent; phone wait times are often shorter than in-person lines during mass cancellations. Screenshot your original itinerary and confirmation number. If your connection is now unreachable, ask specifically about rebooking on partner airlines, not just their own next flight. Check if the cancellation qualifies you for a hotel or meal voucher under the airline's policy — ask directly, they won't always offer. Finally, keep your original boarding pass; you may need it for reimbursement claims later."}
{"prompt": "Can you help me write a polite but firm email to my landlord about a broken heater it's been a week?", "response": "Subject: Heater Repair – Follow-Up Needed

Hi Marcus,

I'm writing to follow up on the broken heater in my unit, which has now been out for a full week despite my initial report last Tuesday. With temperatures dropping, this is becoming a real habitability concern, not just an inconvenience.

Could you let me know today when a repair technician can come by? If this can't be resolved within 48 hours, I'll need to look into tenant remedies available under local housing code, which I'd rather avoid.

I appreciate your quick attention to this.

Thanks,
Dana"}
{"prompt": "I need to pack for a 10-day trip to Iceland in October but only have a carry-on. Help me figure out what to bring.", "response": "October in Iceland means layers, wind, and rain — pack for versatility, not volume. Base: 3 merino or synthetic long-sleeve tops (they don't smell after repeat wear), 2 fleece or wool mid-layers, one real waterproof (not water-resistant) shell jacket and pants. Bring 4-5 pairs of wool socks, quick-dry underwear, and one warm hat plus gloves. Waterproof hiking boots are non-negotiable; everything else can be sneakers for travel days. Skip cotton entirely — it stays wet. Roll clothes, use packing cubes, and wear your bulkiest layer (boots, jacket) on the plane. Add a dry bag for electronics near waterfalls, and you're set."}
</tool_response>

{"prompt": "My 8-year-old keeps getting into arguments with their sibling over screen time and I'm sick of refereeing. What's an approach that actually teaches them to negotiate rather than just imposing rules?", "response": "Try shifting from referee to facilitator. Here's a framework that works: 1) Each Friday, hold a 15-minute 'family council' where both kids propose their screen-time plan for the week. 2) Write the proposals down — kids take things more seriously when it's in writing. 3) Give them a shared budget: e.g., 7 hours total for the week to divide between them however they choose. This forces them to negotiate WITH each other, not through you. 4) During disputes, don't solve it — ask: 'What's your proposal? Have you asked them what they think? What's a fair compromise?' 5) If they DO reach an agreement on their own, acknowledge it specifically: 'You two figured that out yourselves — that's mature.' Over 3-4 weeks, you'll notice them settling disagreements without calling you. The key insight: kids don't mind rules as much as they mind feeling powerless. Give them power within boundaries, and you remove the fight."}
ENTRY

</function>

{"prompt": "I found a strange white powder in my garden soil near my tomato plants. Is this dangerous? What could it be?", "response": "Most likely you're seeing one of three harmless things: (1) mineral deposits from hard water — if you've been watering regularly, calcium/magnesium can crust on the surface; (2) fungal mycelium — look for thread-like structures, which actually means your soil ecosystem is healthy; (3) salt buildup from fertilizer over-application. Here's how to tell: Sprinkle a drop of vinegar on it. If it fizzes, it's lime/mineral deposits (totally fine). If nothing happens and it looks web-like, it's fungus (also fine). If it's crystalline and gritty, it's salt — in that case, flush the soil with plain water for 10 minutes to rinse it out. The only red flag would be if the powder smells chemical or if your plants are also yellowing/dying — then you might have a pesticide residue issue. Based on your description, this sounds completely normal for a home garden."}
ENTRY
</parameter>
</function>

Here's a motivation-first approach: Week 1-2: Learn exactly ONE song you love — pick something with 3-4 chords (most pop/folk songs work). Learn those chords cold (look up chord diagrams, practice switching between them slowly with a metronome at 60 BPM). Once you can play the chord progression without stopping, you'll feel real progress because you can actually MAKE MUSIC. Week 3: Add strumming. Learn one strum pattern (down-down-down-up-up-down-up) and play your song all the way through, even if it's messy. Record yourself on your phone. Week 4: Learn a second song. Compare the recording from week 3 to week 4 — you'll hear improvement and that's the dopamine hit that keeps you going. After 2 months, NOW start learning scales, because you'll understand WHY they matter. The secret: musicians don't quit because it's hard; they quit because they can't hear themselves improving. Force yourself to make music first, theory follows."}
ENTRY

</function>

Here's exactly what to do instead: 1) Open your banking app directly (the one you already have installed) or go to your bank's official website by typing the URL yourself — never use links from texts/emails. 2) Log in and check your account status. If it were actually locked, you'd see it right there in your app. 3) Call the number on the BACK of your debit card — not any number in the text. Ask a human if there's any issue with your account. 99.9% chance this is a phishing scam. Red flags: urgency ('verify NOW or we'll freeze'), threats, links from text messages, generic greetings ('Dear Customer'). Banks NEVER handle security issues through text links. Pro tip going forward: add this number to your speed dial right now: [your bank's real customer service number]. Next time anything like this happens, call that number first. And if you already clicked the link: change your password immediately and enable two-factor authentication if you haven't already."}
ENTRY
